🇺🇸 Pentagon to livestream a firing squad execution

The US military plans to livestream the December 3 execution by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former Army psychiatrist convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that people around the world will be able to watch. The Pentagon said President Donald Trump had given the go-ahead for Hasan to face a firing squad.

If carried out, it would be the first known time US authorities have broadcast an execution live to the public, the first US military execution since 1961, and the first military death by firing squad since World War II. The last legal public execution in the United States took place in 1936.

Legal experts say the broadcast could breach the ban on degrading punishment in an international convention Washington ratified in 1992, as well as US laws on transmitting graphic material to minors. The Army's own justice code bars minors from witnessing an execution. Democrats have called the plan medieval.

Imagine if Russia or China announced that. A state execution by firing squad, broadcast live to the world on the orders of the defense minister. There would be emergency sessions, sanctions packages and weeks of headlines about barbarism and the collapse of human rights.

📡 Aggressive US military bears responsibility for regional maritime escalation: IRGC

📌 Tehran, IRNA — The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy says the US military must be blamed for the escalation of tensions in the regional shipping routes, announcing a new fire incident on a tanker attempting to pass through an illegal route south of the Strait of Hormuz.

In a statement on Friday, the IRGC Navy said a large liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) carrier was struck while attempting to transit the unauthorized route, resulting in a massive fire in its engine room and propulsion system.
​
It held the US military directly responsible for the incident and escalating maritime tensions, arguing that Washington causes such incidents by interfering in and deceiving shipping and insurance companies and by paying large bribes to them.
​
The IRGC Navy said its forces were exercising control over the Strait of Hormuz in line with the order of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Sayyid Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei, and the Iranian people’s demand for sovereignty over the waterway.
​
Pleading that the Iranian forces have not permitted and will not permit the presence of aggressive militaries in the region and that they would decisively deal with any hostile attempts to disrupt the management of the Strait of Hormuz, the statement warned that such bitter incidents would only increase should the American interventions continue.
​
The force also threatened companies with sanctions and punitive measures if their vessels were found in violation after being misled by the US military in the region.
​
Action taken against offending vessels will not be limited to the Strait of Hormuz, but any vessel traversing an unauthorized route anywhere in the region will be pursued and will be punished inevitably, the statement added.

💬 Iranian, Turkmen presidents meet on sidelines of CIS summit in Turkmenistan

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has met with his Turkmen counterpart Serdar Berdimuhamedov on the sidelines of the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) summit.

During the meeting on Friday, the two sides exchanged views on ways to develop and deepen mutual ties in various political, economic, and trade fields.
​
Pezeshkian and Berdimuhamedov also called for strengthening joint cooperation and stressed the need to accelerate the implementation of the agreed projects to expand bilateral ties.
​
They also exchanged views on regional cooperation and Caspian Sea-related issues, with both sides emphasizing the importance of strengthening cooperation among Caspian littoral states, protecting the sea’s environment, and developing joint interactions in line with the interests of the regional countries.
